extracted.intended_audience: USDA policymakers and researchers; National Agricultural Research and Extension Users Advisory Board; analysts of grant funding for rural development
extracted.subtask_short: inventory of foundation grants for RD R/E
extracted.subtask_description: Compile and analyze foundation grant activity supporting rural development research and education (R/E) by searching the Foundation Grants Index and reporting counts, dollar totals, averages, donor/recipient concentrations, geographic distribution, and sample project types for 1972-1980.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period for inventory
rubrics_metrics.description: Search and analysis cover the period 1972-80; the search was conducted Aug. 28, 1980 and the latest grant listed was made in May, 1980.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All grants within 1972-1980 inclusive were considered; report totals, averages, and year-by-year breakdowns for that interval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data source
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary data source was the computerized Foundation Grants Index data base, supplemented by study of the printed version of the Foundation Grants Index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with a broad automated database search (example term used: 'community and rural development'), then narrow results; document search terms, dates searched, and any supplemental sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject inclusion: Rural Development R/E
rubrics_metrics.description: Search was narrowed to 'research or educational grants' within the broader 'community & rural development' subject, then further limited to Rural Development research/education aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only grants explicitly categorized as research or educational and judged to address rural development R/E aspects were included; record how subject narrowing was performed and how ambiguous hits were resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetary inclusion threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants of $5,000 or more were included in the inventory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude grants below the $5,000 threshold; state the cutoff clearly when reporting totals and counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic classification rule (domestic vs foreign)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants classified as 'foreign' include grants made to U.S. recipients if the grant was to be used in a project in a specified country or region other than the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify by project location rather than recipient domicile; provide examples (e.g., Harvard Univ. received Ford funds for field research in Andhra Pradesh, India — counted as foreign).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting repeated grants and multi-year grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Some projects received more than one grant in more than one year; such grants are counted as separate grants in the inventory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and count each grant record separately even if to the same project across years; note aggregated amounts by recipient and by project as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic quantitative metrics to report
rubrics_metrics.description: Report number of grants, total dollar amounts, average grant size, largest single grant, and yearly totals and counts (for domestic and foreign categories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide summary statistics (totals, averages, maxima) and year-by-year breakdowns; the paper reports examples such as domestic total $7,982,986, foreign total $12,913,203, average domestic grant $197,707, average foreign grant $184,474, largest domestic grant $958,585, largest foreign grant $2,250,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal comparison metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare averages across time slices, e.g., even- vs odd-numbered years and subperiods (1972-75 vs 1976-80).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute period averages and comment on differences (paper reports domestic average assistance per year $886,998; even-numbered year average $1,466,889; odd-numbered year average $162,135; 1976-80 five-year average $1,180,775; 1972-75 four-year average $519,778).

rubrics_metrics.name: Donor concentration and share metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the proportion of grants and funding provided by leading donors and report concentration (e.g., percent of grants and percent of funding from top foundations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify top donors and their dollar contributions and compute share of total grants and funding (example: domestically, 39% of the grants and 70% of funding came from Kellogg and Ford; for foreign grants, 94% of grants and 98% of funding were from Ford, Rockefeller and Kellogg).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient concentration and major recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify recipients receiving large cumulative support (e.g., recipients receiving more than $1 million over the period) and report amounts by recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List major recipients and their totals (examples: Washington State Univ. $2,015,486; Mississippi Action for Community Education $1,865,250; Southwest State Univ. Foundation $1,365,917).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic/country distribution of foreign grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Report which countries or regions were the ultimate beneficiaries of foreign grants and identify leading countries by dollar terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a country list and dollar totals; the paper names Canada, Brazil, Bangladesh, India and Indonesia as leading recipients in dollar terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project type categorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize funded projects by type (examples include matching funds, leadership training, community development activities, public policy resources and research, management skills instruction, educational/health/agricultural services, research design and investigation, social science training aimed at raising incomes, research on local indicators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sample descriptions of project aims and use these categories to summarize the kinds of R/E activities funded; include representative grant descriptions as illustrative examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison with government spending
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide context by comparing foundation funding totals to government sector expenditures on community and rural development (examples: Cooperative Extension Service spending approx. $62,744,000 and Cooperative State Research $15,224,000 in FY 1979).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting foundation grant totals, include comparable government expenditure figures to situate foundation activity within the broader funding landscape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search narrowing and review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological workflow: initial broad automated search produced >3,000 hits for 'community and rural development', narrowed to 872 citations for 'research or educational grants', then limited to Rural Development R/E aspects producing 108 items printed for senior author review; junior author conducted the search and senior author analyzed the items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document each narrowing step, the persons responsible for search vs analysis, and the criteria used to reduce hits; keep a reproducible trail of search terms, counts at each stage, and reasons for exclusion.
